clue.text: Annual celebration always introduced by pig farmer?

indicators.note: the word for always comes after, being led in by, the farmer piece

parts.note: a man who keeps hogs could whimsically be called a hog-man
aye, spelt ay, is an old word for always or ever

explanation.surface: A farmer who raises pigs is asked to open some yearly festivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced by' puts the farmer first. Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year festivity, held every year on the last night of December.

clue.text: Mother leaving capital with husband's pet rodent

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: the mother word leaves, is taken from, the capital

parts.note: Amsterdam is the capital of the Netherlands
a dam is a mother, usually of an animal

explanation.surface: A mother leaves the capital with her husband's pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamsters are small rodents commonly kept as pets.

clue.text: Paper over something fishy here

indicators.note: in a down clue, the paper word is turned over, read upwards

parts.note: a rag is slang for a cheap newspaper

explanation.surface: Something suspicious is being covered over in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' looks like suspicious, but it is literal: a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted fish, also called garfish or needlefish.

clue.text: Like the aims of a companion that's very clever?

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
i.e., that is, is the Latin abbreviation id est
an able person is clever

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a very clever companion has goals like these.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is short: aims that can be reached.
explanation.definitionFit: Good aims are ones that can be reached or realised, attainable goals.

clue.text: He wrote a work about El Salvador's leaders

indicators.note: the letters A and OP go round the leading letters

parts.note: op, for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: the leaders of El Salvador are its first letters, E and S

explanation.surface: A writer produces a book about the rulers of El Salvador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks political, but it takes initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of animal fables.

clue.text: Girl's way to get round a monitor, perhaps

parts.note: Liz is a common girl's name, short for Elizabeth
RD is the standard abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A girl takes a detour to avoid some computer screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The monitor here is a large reptile, not a screen; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a large tropical reptile, one example of the scaly family it belongs to.

clue.text: Holly's former partner ——— in Paris he's at the top

indicators.note: in a down answer the French word sits above, at the top

parts.note: il is French for he
an ex is a former partner or spouse

explanation.surface: Holly's ex-partner is now top man in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: Holly reads as a woman's name; the 's is 'is', the plant being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the botanical genus name for the holly plants.

clue.text: Like a plant? A graduate managed yours once

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a graduate
to run a business is to manage it
thine is the old form of yours

explanation.surface: A graduate once ran your plant affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaranthine describes the amaranth, an imaginary unfading flower, so it is plant-like.

clue.text: Infirm stranger visiting outskirts of Derby

indicators.note: the word for stranger comes into the outskirts
the outskirts are the outer letters, D and Y

parts.note: odder means more strange

explanation.surface: A frail stranger is visiting the edge of Derby, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a person, but it is a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery describes someone shaky and feeble, especially with age.

clue.text: Fearful old American associated with Asian island

parts.note: Timor is an island in the Malay archipelago
US stands for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: An old American is anxious about an Asian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Timorous means timid and easily frightened, full of fear.

clue.text: Island trade centre owns cart reversing outside plant

parts.note: a mart is a market, a centre of trade

indicators.note: the owning word and the turned cart sit either side of, outside, the plant

parts.note: to own something is to have it: he has

indicators.note: the word for cart is read backwards, as a cart can reverse

parts.note: a dray is a low heavy cart, as for brewers' barrels
a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A trading post owns a cart which backs out past some plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns DRAY into YARD; 'outside' puts HAS and YARD either side of VINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is a holiday island off the coast of Massachusetts.

clue.text: Noble past ordinand originally working as server

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a new arrangement
only the opening letter of ordinand is taken

explanation.surface: An aristocratic former trainee priest now works as a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives O from ordinand; with NOBLE and PAST, 'working' rearranges the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spoon used to serve food at the table is a serving implement.

clue.text: Girl mounting horse in spring, one that hunts, naturally

indicators.note: the girl and horse pieces go inside the word for spring

parts.note: a bound is a spring or leap

indicators.note: in a down clue, the girl's name climbs, read upwards

parts.note: Tessa is a girl's name
H is slang for heroin, which is called horse

explanation.surface: A girl mounts a horse in springtime and goes hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns TESSA into ASSET; 'horse' is heroin, H, not a riding animal. Spring is a leap, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged scent hound bred to hunt, so hunting comes by instinct.

clue.text: Assignation that may be fruitful

definitions.meaning: an arranged meeting, especially a romantic one
the sweet brown fruit of a palm

explanation.surface: A romantic meeting might bear fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a romantic appointment and the palm's sweet fruit share this one word.

clue.text: One may circumvent obstacles to get on air trip

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall into new order

explanation.surface: Someone getting round obstacles to arrange a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like a journey by air, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal-maker works around difficulties between parties to reach agreement.

clue.text: Begin again, making engineers jump

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
to start is to jump suddenly in surprise

explanation.surface: Something is begun a second time and the engineers jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart something is to set it going once more after a stop.

clue.text: Rented accommodation several fellows used in film

parts.note: ten stands for an unspecified several

indicators.note: the men are put inside the film title

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Several men were cast in a film about rented housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building of rented flats or apartments.

clue.text: Deliveries left in tatty wrappers for all to see

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, six deliveries

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left goes inside the outer letters
the wrappers of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Parcels are left in shabby packaging where everyone can see them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrappers' takes T and Y from tatty, and 'in' puts L between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly, where anyone may watch, is doing it in plain view.

clue.text: Cause of trouble, good king abandoning citadel

indicators.note: the king letter leaves the citadel word

parts.note: the Kremlin is the citadel at the heart of Moscow
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Trouble comes when a good monarch leaves his fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for unexplained faults in machinery.

clue.text: Exuberantly joyous, like a book of part-songs?

definitions.meaning: a glee is an unaccompanied part-song, so a book of them is full of glees

explanation.surface: A songbook full of harmonies is a merry thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of delight in one reading; full of part-songs in the whimsical other.

clue.text: For example, scoops one used in shops

indicators.note: the numeral is put inside the word for shops

parts.note: stores are shops
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Scoops of ice cream are an example of what shops use.
explanation.walkthrough: The scoops are exclusive news reports, not ice cream portions.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive news item, so scoops are examples of news reports.

clue.text: It's acceptable, actor having left for meet

indicators.note: the actor's letters have left the longer word

parts.note: satisfactory means acceptable
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor quit to go to a meeting, which is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet a need or a requirement is to fulfil it.

clue.text: Genuine old railway initially shunned by German dramatist

indicators.note: the railway letters are dropped from the start of the dramatist's name

parts.note: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright
BR is British Rail, the former national railway

explanation.surface: A German playwright initially snubbed an old railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: British Rail ran Britain's trains until privatisation in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword meaning authentic or real.

clue.text: Unashamed declaration of writer beginning to imbibe wine

parts.note: a pen announcing itself would say I'm pen

indicators.note: just the first letter of imbibe is taken

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, mostly used for communion

explanation.surface: A writer declares an intention to start drinking wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is the pen itself, speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unrepentant feels no remorse, and so is not ashamed.

clue.text: Impish female trapped by rising river

indicators.note: the female letter is held inside the river
in a down clue, the river rises, read upwards

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A mischievous woman is caught by a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means like an elf, small and mischievous.

clue.text: Old garden in walled enclosure

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the words walled enclosure

explanation.surface: An ancient garden lies inside a walled plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden where Adam and Eve lived is the first garden of all.

clue.text: They originated in America in 1787

parts.note: the delegates who drew up the US Constitution in 1787 began the nation, as if they had fathered it

explanation.definitionFit: The men who drafted the US Constitution in 1787 are honoured as the nation's creators.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher tells it regularly

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A prophet's tutor tells the story regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the boy Samuel was brought up by the priest Eli.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli the priest raised and instructed Samuel at the temple of Shiloh.

clue.text: Criminal racket breaking into this cargo

indicators.note: the noise word goes inside the criminal word

parts.note: an old lag is a hardened criminal, a convict
din is a loud racket, noise

explanation.surface: A criminal gang breaks into the freight on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' looks like a criminal scheme, but it is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Lading is the load or freight carried aboard a ship, as in bill of lading.

clue.text: Outrageous act, dropping soldiers into hostile state!

indicators.note: the soldiers go inside the word for hostility

parts.note: enmity is a state of hostility
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers are dropped into an enemy country, an outrageous act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' is just the act of putting the soldiers in.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a grave wrong or atrocity, a monstrously wicked deed.
